` and keeps its id until the next\n upload restores it.\n* **Uploads are budgeted** per person and server: 60, refilling at 120 a

n
 hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

### Who can upload

An API key acts as the person who created it,
with all of that person's\naccess. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated member who\nis not a project admin, s
o a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\nserver shared with the project, accounts are project accounts: only a project\na

dmin can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Running evals as an account

A run
with no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.\nTo run evals from CI as one account, upload its token, mak

e it the default,
then start the run:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PATCH \
 "https://app.mcpj
am.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KE

Y" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The CLI takes the same steps with `mcpj
am cloud server-accounts set`, which\nreads the token from a file, an environment variable or stdin, and\n`mcpjam cloud server-acc

ounts default`. See the
[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-accounts-commands).

The default
is shared by every run that key starts, so don't run the same\nkey's runs at the same time with different defaults. A suite that h
as saved\naccounts in its settings runs as those accounts and ignores the default, so\ncheck the suite's settings before relying o

n the default.

### Deleting an account

`DELETE` removes the account and its stored token, and asks the token's issuer
to re
voke the token where the issuer supports revocation. That is best effort,\nand it also ends any copy of the same token you still h

old. The default
account can't be deleted while other accounts exist (`409`): make another
account the default first.

### The

deprecated import route

`POST .../oauth/import-tokens` still works, and is removed 90 days after the
accounts API shipped. It
uploads to your default account, creating an unnamed\none when the server has none, and keeps its old body and its old\n`{ import

ed, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carries `Deprecation: true`, a
`Sunset` date and a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An account
this route creates is hosted-only. An existing default it writes\ninto keeps whatever rule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the URL
saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`\nand `tokens.id_token` are accepted a

nd ignored. Move to
`PUT .../accounts/{account}`, which names the account it writes.

The error codes these routes add to `deta
ils.code` are listed in the\n[error code reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors).

## Run evals from the API

The shortest useful loop: create a run with one inline test, then poll:

```bash theme={"theme
\":\"css-variables\"}\n# 1. Create (responds 202 immediately; -f + jq -e fail fast on errors)\nRUN_ID=$(curl -fsS -X POST \\\n \"
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Conte

nt-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{
 "suiteName": "smoke",
 "serverIds": ["'$SERVER_ID'"],
 "tests": [{\

n "title": "echo works",
 "runs": 1,
 "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5",
 "provider": "ant

hropic",
 "steps": [
 { "id": "s1", "kind": "prompt", "prompt": "Use the echo tool to say hi" },
p.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\"\n\n# 3. If it did
not pass, read the decision summary FIRST\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/decision
-summary\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\"\n\n# 4. Or go straight to per-iteration tool calls, token usage, lat
ency\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/iterations\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer

$MCPJAM_API_KEY"
```

The decision summary composes steps 2 and 4 into one versioned object so every
client reads a run the

same way. Four things to know before gating on it:

* **`measurementUnit` ships with every count.** Under per-case grading the
counts are case-execution *variants*, with iterations as trials inside them;\n under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are t
rials. The same suite reports\n a different total under each, 3 against 15 for three cases run five times,\n so a count without
its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never converted\n across that line.\n* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides it.**
The run's own decision is\n the authority and is carried through on `decision`. The per-trial\n `diagnostics` sit underneath it
. A case can pass with a failing trial in it,\n so tallying diagnostics gives a different answer than the platform reached.\n* **
`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a failure and not `inconclusive`.** It\n means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped
early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.reason` says which. `inconclusive` *is* a decision; the validity\n phase ran and withheld
a verdict.\n* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether you have the whole list.** A page\n fetched with a `cursor` is never complete

, and `scannedIterations` separates
 "nothing failed" from "we did not look".

Evidence is scoped to the claim it supports
: for a measured failure the span\nids, prompt indexes and reasons come from the first failed stage's row alone,\nand `evidence.tr

acePath` is an API-relative path you can append to your base URL
to read the full trace.

`model` takes an id from the hosted c
atalog (`provider/name` form, e.g.\n`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`) and runs on your organization's credits.\nProvider-native ids (e
.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pass\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't execute is rejected at\ncr

eate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedModels` lists the valid
hosted ids for that provider.

Reruns are even shorte
r: `{ \"suiteId\": \"...\" }` reruns the suite exactly as\nconfigured, connecting the suite's saved server selection (the `202` re
sponse\nlists the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverIds` to override the selection; a\nsuite with no saved selection requires it (`

VALIDATION_ERROR` with
`details.reason: "NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running against a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is launchable only through a suite that has
it **attached**. Attach them first with
`PATCH
/projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`\narray (send `null` to detach them all; `[]` is rejected, us
e `null`), then\npass `environmentId` on the run. It must be one of that suite's attached\nenvironments; anything else is a `400`

with
`details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED"`, raised before any case is
authored or any server connected.

Omitting `en
vironmentId` is meaningful, and depends on the suite:\n\n* **no** attached environments → the run uses the saved server selection,
as before;\n* **exactly one** attached → that environment is used automatically. The `202`\n response's `environment` field says

so;
* **several** attached → `400` with `details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED"`,
 naming the candidates.

The environment
supplies the closed server set, so `serverIds` is not required and is\n**rejected** alongside it (`400`), rather than accepted an
d ignored: honoring\nboth would connect a different set than the run is stamped with. The same goes\nfor a `serverIds` override on
